name: Bosnian Ćevapi
description: Ćevapi, small grilled minced-meat fingers, is Bosnia's beloved national dish - real technique kneads the meat with a little baking soda, which is what gives real ćevapi their genuinely bouncy, springy texture, and lets the mixture rest (traditionally 24-48 hours) so it becomes cohesive rather than a loose mince. Real technique shapes them into small, finger-sized logs, not full patties.
steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the garlic, baking soda, pepper, and salt, kneading by hand 5-6 minutes until it becomes cohesive and slightly tacky - this real kneading and the baking soda together are what build real ćevapi's springy texture.
Cover tightly and refrigerate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight, so the mixture firms up and the flavors meld.
Shape into small finger-sized logs, about 2 inches long.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 6-8 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Bosnian Burek
description: Burek, a spiral savory pastry with a meat filling, depends on real paper-thin, hand-stretched dough (jufka) - this version uses phyllo as the practical substitute, real technique rolling the filled dough into a tight coil rather than folding it flat.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion until soft, 3-4 minutes, then add the beef and pepper and brown, 6-7 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
Brush each phyllo sheet with oil, spread a thin layer of the meat filling along one edge, and roll into a tight log.
Coil the rolled log into a tight spiral in a round baking dish, alongside additional coiled logs to fill the pan.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 30-35 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Bosnian Ajvar
description: Ajvar, a roasted red pepper and eggplant relish, is a genuine Balkan staple and the real, traditional accompaniment to ćevapi, real technique roasting both vegetables until the skins char fully for real smoky depth.
steps_detailed: Roast the bell pepper and eggplant at 450F (230C) for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the skins are fully charred and blistered.
Let cool slightly, then peel off the skins.
Blend or mash the roasted vegetables with the garlic, olive oil, and vinegar until mostly smooth but still a little textured.

name: Bosnian Somun
description: Somun, a soft, slightly chewy flatbread, is the real, traditional bread served alongside ćevapi, real technique letting the dough rise properly before baking for its distinctive pillowy texture.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and baking powder with warm water into a soft dough.
Let rest 30-40 minutes until slightly puffed.
Shape into a round, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and bake at 425F (220C) for 12-15 minutes until golden and pillowy.

name: Bosnian Sarma
description: Sarma, cabbage leaves stuffed with rice and meat, is a genuine Bosnian and wider Balkan staple, real technique using well-softened, pliable cabbage leaves so they roll without tearing.
steps_detailed: Blanch the cabbage leaves 3-4 minutes until fully pliable.
Mix the raw rice with the beef and onion.
Roll a spoonful of the filling tightly into each cabbage leaf.
Arrange in a pot, cover with the tomatoes and enough water to just cover, and simmer 40-45 minutes until the rice is tender.

name: Bosnian Bosanski Lonac
description: Bosanski lonac, a real layered meat and vegetable pot, is a genuine Bosnian one-pot staple, real technique layering the ingredients rather than stirring them together, letting each cook in the steam of the one below.
steps_detailed: Layer the beef, onion, carrot, cabbage, and potato in a heavy pot without stirring.
Add enough water to reach partway up the layers.
Cover and simmer very gently, without stirring, 1.5-2 hours, until everything is tender - real bosanski lonac depends on this undisturbed layering.

name: Bosnian Cucumber Tomato Salad (Shopska-Style)
description: A simple, bright cucumber and tomato salad topped with real crumbled cheese, shared across the wider Balkans.
steps_detailed: Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the olive oil.
Top with the crumbled feta.

name: Bosnian Roasted Peppers
description: Roasted red peppers dressed simply with olive oil and garlic are a beloved Bosnian side, real technique charring the skin fully so it peels away cleanly.
steps_detailed: Roast the peppers at 450F (230C) for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the skin is fully charred and blistered.
Let cool slightly, then peel off the skin and slice.
Toss with the garlic and olive oil.

name: Bosnian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Bosnia's rivers and coastal Adriatic influence.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Bosnian Roasted Walnuts
description: A simple roasted walnut snack, common across Bosnia.
steps_detailed: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Bosnian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Bosnian home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Bosnian Sour Cream Sauce (Kajmak-Style)
description: A simple, rich sour cream sauce echoing the flavor of kajmak, Bosnia's traditional clotted-cream-like dairy product, served alongside ćevapi.
steps_detailed: Whisk the sour cream with the salt and chill before serving.
